discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 061717
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
1217 PM EST Fri Nov 6 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Scattered to numerous lake effect rain showers today into
  tonight, mainly for areas west of Interstate 69 in northern IN
  and southwest MI.

- Cool and breezy today into Saturday with highs near 50 degrees.

- Dry and warmer than average weather returns early next week.

&&

.UPDATE...
Issued at 1054 AM EST Fri Nov 6 2026

Somewhat more organized lake effect band trying to take shape
from northern St Joseph county in Indiana to Berrien county and
along the eastern shore of Lk MI. The upper level trough has
passed through with some slightly better convergence underway to
aid in development. Hi res models continue to waver some on
final resting position of the band and how far inland. Did make
a few changes on alignment of pops and increase to cat for areas
most likely to remain under the band. While a downward trend is
reflected later today, additional changes may be needed as there
continues to be indications of more waves dropping south and
continued development until both the flow, inversion heights and
RH become less favorable.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 316 AM EST Fri Nov 6 2026

Areas of light rain and drizzle associated with a positively 
tilted upper trough and cold front should exit eastern zones by
12z. Today into tonight then features a transition to lake 
enhanced/effect rain showers thanks to ongoing cold advection 
within deepening north-northwest flow. This occurs on the 
backside of a potent vort lobe dropping southeast through the 
central/eastern Great Lakes. More intense banding may set up for
a time in sw MI and nc IN later this morning through this 
evening as the prevailing flow becomes parallel to the long axis
of Lake MI resulting in stronger frictional/thermal convergence
over eastern Lake MI. Localized rainfall amounts may exceed a 
half inch in spots, best chances Berrien MI down into 
LaPorte/South Bend/Plymouth. Drying and subsidence eventually 
takes its toll on inversion heights by later tonight and 
Saturday bringing an end to more organized LE rain. Cooler and 
somewhat breezy early November wx otherwise today into Saturday.

Flow regime flattens out Sunday into early next week with more 
active westerlies shifting off to the north-northeast. Return west-
southwest flow will usher in a milder pacific air mass with 
sunshine and warm advection resulting in a return to above 
normal temps. Some degree of upper troughing and CAA then
settles back in for the second half of next week with near 
normal temps and non-zero rain shower chances.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z SATURDAY/...
Issued at 1213 PM EST Fri Nov 6 2026

Northwesterly flow will continue to produce light lake effect 
rain showers to areas downstream from Lake Michigan. Therefore, keep
MVFR cigs through Saturday morning for KSBN. With the lake 
effect showers remaining west of KFWA did keep the forecast dry,
although MVFR ceilings are forecast late tonight/early Saturday. 
Winds will increase this afternoon with gusts around 20 kts 
possible, than decrease again to around 10 kts or less overnight.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory until 4 PM EST Saturday for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

UPDATE...Fisher
DISCUSSION...Steinwedel
AVIATION...Cobb

spc.text:
SPC AC 061556

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0956 AM CST Fri Nov 06 2026

   Valid 061630Z - 071200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS THIS AFTERNOON
   ACROSS PARTS OF EASTERN NORTH CAROLINA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms may occur today across parts
   of the central/eastern Carolinas and coastal southern Mid-Atlantic.

   ...Eastern NC...
   An upper low over lower MI and an associated upper trough extending
   southward through the OH/TN valleys will track eastward today,
   providing large-scale forcing for ascent across much of the eastern
   states.  A cluster of thunderstorms that began several hours ago in
   northern SC is progressing northeastward across central NC.  Cloud
   cover ahead of this activity is limiting daytime
   heating/destabilization.  However, dewpoints near 70F and cooling
   aloft will likely lead to a narrow corridor of MUCAPE values of
   around 1500 J/kg this afternoon.  CAM guidance is in agreement that
   there will be a period of vigorous convection over eastern NC in the
   19-23z time period.  Low-level winds are somewhat veered and not
   particularly strong.  However, stronger winds aloft and the
   approaching upper trough may result in sufficient organization for a
   few bowing structures capable damaging wind gusts and some hail.  A
   small SLGT risk has been added to address this focused risk area.

   ...Southeast AZ...
   A strong thunderstorm or two may occur this afternoon over extreme
   southeast AZ, in a steep lapse-rate and marginally unstable
   environment.  While hail will be possible in the strongest cores,
   the threat appears too minimal for severe probabilities at this
   time.

   ..Hart/Kerr.. 11/06/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 2000Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 061700

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1100 AM CST Fri Nov 06 2026

   Valid 071200Z - 081200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not forecast across the U.S. Saturday and
   Saturday night.

   ...Synopsis...

   An upper cyclone and attendant trough will pivot east/northeast
   across the Mid-Atlantic and Northeast on Saturday. A cold front will
   have already moved offshore most of the Atlantic coast by Saturday
   morning, except perhaps over far eastern portions of New England.
   Isolated thunderstorm may occur within the warm conveyor ahead of
   the upper cyclone, though severe storms are not expected. 

   Additional, and more widespread showers and thunderstorms are
   expected across portions of southern/central TX within a low-level
   warm advection regime ahead of a developing upper cyclone across
   northern Mexico. Instability will remain too meager to support
   severe convection.

   A few lightning flashes also will be possible across parts of the
   Pacific Northwest and strong southwesterly flow overspread the
   region ahead of an approaching upper shortwave trough and cold front
   late in the forecast period. Gusty winds may accompany convection as
   it moves onshore given the strength of background synoptic flow, but
   MUCAPE less than 200 J/kg will preclude severe convection.

   ..Leitman.. 11/06/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 0700Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 060724

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0124 AM CST Fri Nov 06 2026

   Valid 081200Z - 091200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   No severe threat is forecast across the continental U.S. Sunday and
   Sunday night.

   ...DISCUSSION...
   Northwest flow at mid-levels is expected on Sunday from the
   north-central states to the Eastern Seaboard. Further southwest, an
   upper-level low is forecast to move toward the Rio Grande Valley of
   southwest Texas. A moist airmass will likely be located over south
   and central Texas, where scattered to numerous thunderstorms will be
   possible during the day. Thunderstorms may continue across parts of
   south Texas in the overnight period. Instability is forecast to be
   weak across south and central Texas, making severe thunderstorm
   development unlikely. Elsewhere across the continental U.S.,
   thunderstorms are not expected Sunday and Sunday night.

   ..Broyles.. 11/06/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
